title: utilz liberator: brew check ignores utilz's own use switch, so a dev or opt link set reads as an unnamed fault
body:
## What happened (rhadamanth, 25 Oct 2026)

hv's `molt resleeve` failed the utilz liberator: "utilz (brew): PATH runs /Users/matts/.local/bin/utilz (utilz 2.14.3 (dev, 21b0385de0bb) at /Users/matts/Devel/prj/Utilz), not Homebrew's /opt/homebrew/bin/utilz", and the same for every utility.

The cause: 18 links in `~/.local/bin` into `~/Devel/prj/Utilz/bin`, dated 22 Sep, left by Molt's old checkout mode. They were shadowed while Homebrew's `bin` led PATH. Molt-matts' PATH change of 24-25 Oct (91a71ff, a258ad0: `~/.local/bin` first, hv's ruling B under devbin's dev/opt/brew contract T5) put them first. Utilz reads exactly that link set as its own switch: `utilz use` answers "dev at /Users/matts/Devel/prj/Utilz -- 18 link(s)". hv ruled brew for rhadamanth (20 Oct, again 25 Oct) and runs `utilz use brew`.

## The defect

Under the contract, each tool's per-user link set in `~/.local/bin` is the switch, and the tool's own `use` verb is the one thing that sets and reports it (T5). Molt's utilz liberator does not know that switch exists. In `source = "brew"` it asks only whether PATH runs Homebrew's copy, so a deliberate `utilz use dev` reads as a fault with no remedy named, and the message never says the switch is what decides.

## Spec (vc, 25 Oct 2026)

In `liberators/utilz.sh`, the brew-source check asks Utilz's own switch before PATH, in one place:

- When `utilz use` (run by Homebrew's utilz, by path, so a shadowing link cannot answer for itself) reports no link set, the check is the current one: Homebrew's copy must be what PATH runs.
- When it reports a dev or opt link set, the check fails, naming the tree the switch serves and the remedy, `utilz use brew`, since the sleeve declares brew. It does not reclassify the sleeve.
- When `utilz use` itself fails, or reports shadowing, its words are shown and the check fails.

`utilz_install` never runs `utilz use`: moving a user's switch is the user's verb, not resleeve's. It reports as above. Checkout mode is untouched. Nothing is written to molt.toml.

Tests fake both brew and Homebrew's `utilz use` (no link set; dev link set; `use` failing), each red with the change reverted. The full suite runs under Homebrew bash and /bin/bash 3.2, plus shellcheck.

## Not in scope

The same switch question for other tools under the contract (intent, gtools): their liberators ask PATH and the gate home today. Whether they should ask their tool's `use` is a later issue.

The live proof is hv's own `utilz use brew` on rhadamanth, run by hv at the keyboard: resleeve never moves the switch, so `molt doctor` reports Homebrew's utilz once hv has moved it.

## As built (dc, 25 Oct 2026; merged and pushed by vc at 60b854f)

- `liberators/utilz.sh`: a new `_utilz_switch_faults` runs Homebrew's `$(brew --prefix)/bin/utilz use` by path, with no word, and `_utilz_brew_faults` asks it before the PATH check. Each `<tree> at <root> -- <n> link(s)` line it reports becomes a fault naming that tree and `'utilz use brew'`. A non-zero exit shows `use`'s own output (its shadowing lines among it), or says it said nothing. With no link set, the PATH check runs as before. A switch fault stands in place of the PATH check, which would only repeat it without the remedy.
- `utilz_install` reports these faults and never moves the switch; Molt calls `use` only with no word. Checkout mode and molt.toml are untouched. The header comment says Molt now asks the bare `use`.
- `test/liberators/utilz.bats`: `_utilz_brew` fakes Homebrew's utilz answering `use` (no link set by default, logging each call), and `_utilz_use` sets what it says next. New tests cover no link set (`use` is asked and the PATH check stands), a dev and an opt link set (check, verify and install fail with the remedy, and nothing but the bare `use` is called), and `use` failing with shadowing words or with no output. Each new test fails with main's liberator restored.
- Read-only against the real `/opt/homebrew/bin/utilz` on rhadamanth, the new function named `dev at /Users/matts/Devel/prj/Utilz` with `'utilz use brew'`, under `use`'s own shadowing lines.
- The full suite passes under Homebrew bash and /bin/bash 3.2, and shellcheck is clean on the liberator.
